lines.text: gift which is given with the intention of committing the
recipient to a sense of material obligation is not a true gift.
It is right to refuse to feel dependent on the calculations of
the other party; but it is not right to resist the sense of
dependence on his kindness.
True giving binds two people together in perfect free-
dom without implying any material obligation of the one
party towards the other. The acceptance of gifts of this kind
requires open-heartedness, glad and spontaneous sub-
mission to the kindness of the giver. And it is just this
attitude which so many people cannot bring themselves to
adopt. They suppose that it means yielding ground too
much and they shut themselves up in an attitude of hard
inaccessibility, from the sheer need to assert their power and
authority. They do not know the happiness that lies precisely
in receiving gifts and thereby winning favour. This is
especially clear from the fact that so many people resist
receiving from others one of the greatest of gifts which a
man can bestow on his neighbour: namely, forgiveness. For
in order that this may come about a man must confess his
wrong to another, and this injures his pride and sense of
deserving. And yet our whole life together as a community
wins freedom and happiness just from the fact that one is
prepared to confess his sin to another and to receive for-
giveness.
In just the same way men spoil their relation to God
because they are not prepared to confess what they truly
are in the sight of God: worthless creatures who have
nothing which they did not receive from Him, creatures
whose lives are without any content or meaning apart from
His grace, and who must flee again and again to His grace
in order to have any value, creatures who can receive trom
Him alone that meaningfulness which frees them from the
tense struggle to assert their value.
"God be merciful to me a sinner!" cries the tax collector.
And Jesus adds: "I tell you this man went down to his house
justified rather than the other." It is just the confession of
sin which frees man from the fetters of self-from himself
